significance: A shrine in central Kathmandu dedicated to Sweta Kali, known among Newars as Nyata Ajima, and believed to have been founded in the ninth century by Gunakamadeva, the founder of the city; its three-tiered roof includes a gilded storey carried on carved struts.
story: A king of Patan who lost his way while hunting and was chased by a wild elephant is said to have hidden in a tree at this spot, where the goddess Swetakali appeared and gave him back his life, upon which he founded the temple.
